response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack/web engineer with some low-level exposure (C/C++ at National Instruments, DLang systems work), but he is fundamentally misaligned with this role. The position requires native-level Japanese, deep C-on-UNIX proficiency, Linux kernel source modification experience, and embedded networking security expertise (MACsec, 802.1X, L2/L3 switching) — none of which appear on the resume. His recent decade of work is web-oriented (TypeScript, Node.js, React), and his listed languages are English, Romanian, and basic German, making the mandatory Japanese requirement an outright disqualifier.
strengths: 18+ years of broad software development experience, well above the 3-year minimum
Some systems-level background: C/C++ at National Instruments, low-latency DLang services, Linux familiarity
Strong engineering practices (TDD, CI/CD) and open-source contributions demonstrating self-direction
concerns: No Japanese language ability, which is a hard requirement (native-level proficiency)
No embedded networking or security-feature experience (MACsec, 802.1X, switch chips, NETCONF/SNMP)
No demonstrated Linux kernel analysis/modification or recent professional C development

key_factors.factor: Long general software engineering track record
